details.availability: Public Swift source built locally with build.sh; decisions require a TypeSafe API key for the hosted Jev model, and planning optionally an OpenRouter key.

code.basis: repository LICENSE header; not a weights/data license

name: jev-use
notes: The Swift app (built as Desktop Voice.app; macOS 14.2+ and Xcode) reads the front window's Accessibility tree, skipping secure text fields, and sends the command, app and window names, numbered targets and recent actions to TypeSafe's hosted systemone endpoint with model jev-latest; no screenshots are sent (Sources/JevDesktop/Desktop.swift, Sources/JevCore/Decision.swift). Actions use Accessibility presses and value setting plus CGEvent mouse, key and scroll events. An optional OpenRouter key enables a planner model (default inception/mercury-2.5) that splits a spoken command into steps; Jev still chooses each on-screen target (Sources/JevCore/Planner.swift). Input is Apple Speech hold-to-talk, hands-free mode, an optional "Hey Jev" wake phrase, or typed commands. The README says low-confidence and destructive picks stop and ask. Jev is a hosted model; its weights are not part of this repository. Code was read, not run.
summary: macOS voice and typed computer-use app that walks the front app's Accessibility tree, has the hosted Jev model pick an operation and a numbered target each step, and acts via Accessibility actions and synthetic input.
